blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) aims to detect anomalies in unseen domains using only a few reference samples. Recent normal-abnormal guided methods improve this setting by exploiting abnormal references, but their residuals often mix transferable anomaly cues with domain-specific appearance factors such as texture, geometry, and acquisition conditions. This residual domain entanglement limits cross-domain transfer and may produce spurious activations on novel domains. We propose DART, a plug-in framework for normal-abnormal guided GAD that learns to separate residuals into anomaly-relevant and domain-specific components. DART combines a Residual Disentanglement Module, which preserves anomaly-discriminative information while suppressing domain information, with Cross-Domain Meta-Training, which forms episodes across source domains to make the separation effective. The method is architecture-agnostic and can be inserted between residual computation and the detection head of existing GAD pipelines. Experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, and BraTS show consistent improvements over multiple base methods, with the largest gains under stronger domain shifts. https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART
blocks.zh: 通用异常检测(GAD)旨在仅利用少数参考样本来检测未见域的异常. 最近的常态-异常制导方法通过利用异常的引用来改进这种设置,但其残留物往往将可转移的异常提示与特定域的外观因素混合在一起,如纹理,几何和获取条件. 这种剩余域缠绕限制了跨域转移,并可能在新域产生虚假的激活. 我们提出DART,这是正常-异常引导的GAD的插件框架,可以学习将残留物分离成异常相关和特定域的组件. DART结合了一个残余分散模块,该模块在压制域信息的同时保存异常-歧视信息,与跨域Meta-Training,它形成跨源域的事件,以使分离有效. 该方法具有架构不可知性,可以在剩余计算和现有GAD管道检测头之间插入. 在MVTec AD,VisA,和BratS上的实验显示,比起多个基方法,在较强域位移下,其收益最大. https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-12-21.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Visual anomaly detection is central to industrial inspection [ 1 , 2 ] , medical diagnosis [ 3 ] , and safety-critical monitoring [ 4 ] . Most existing methods [ 5 , 6 , 7 , 8 , 9 ] train separate models for individual domains, which becomes impractical when new categories appear frequently, labeled data is scarce, or target-domain training is restricted. Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) addresses this limitation by training a unified model on source domains and deploying it on unseen target domains without fine-tuning [ 10 , 11 ] . At inference, the model detects anomalies in a query image by comparing it with a few target-domain references. Early GAD methods, such as InCTRL [ 10 ] and ResAD [ 11 ] , rely only on normal references, assuming that anomalies induce larger residuals relative to normal prototypes.
blocks.zh: 视觉异常检测是工业检查[1,2],医学诊断[3],安全关键监测[4]的中心. 大多数现有方法[5、6、7、8、9]为单个领域培训单独的模型,当新的类别频繁出现时,这些模型变得不切实际,贴有标签的数据稀缺,或者目标领域培训受到限制。 一般异常检测(GAD)通过在源域上培训一个统一的模型,并在不作微调的隐形目标域上部署这个模型来解决这一局限性[10,11]. 推断出,该模型通过将其与少数目标域参考物作比较,在查询图像中检测出异常. 早期的GAD方法,如InCTRL [10]和ResAD [11],只依靠正常的引用,假设异常会诱发与正常原型相比较大的残留.

blocks.en: Recent normal-abnormal guided GAD methods further exploit a small number of abnormal references, which are often available in practical settings. NAGL [ 12 ] , for instance, uses residual mining and anomaly feature learning to transfer abnormal cues from references to queries, improving over normal-only prompting. However, we show that the residuals driving this transfer are often domain-entangled : they mix transferable anomaly cues with domain-specific factors such as texture, object geometry, and acquisition conditions. For example, a cracked-bottle residual encodes both the crack pattern and bottle-specific appearance; when transferred to leather or transistors, such domain-specific information can trigger false activations or suppress genuine anomalies. We call this phenomenon residual domain entanglement and identify it as a key bottleneck for cross-domain normal-abnormal guided GAD (see Figure 1 ).
blocks.zh: 最近的正常-异常的性别与发展方法进一步利用了少数异常的参考,这些参考往往在实际环境中提供。 例如,NAGL [12] 利用剩余采矿和异常特征的学习将异常提示从查询引用中转移,比普通的提示有所改进。 然而,我们表明,驱动这种转让的剩余部分往往被域缠绕:它们将可转移的异常提示与特定域因素相混合,如纹理、对象几何和获取条件。 例如,一个被破解的瓶子残基编码了裂纹图案和瓶子特异的外观;当被转移到皮革或晶体管上时,这种域特异性的信息会触发假活化或压制真正的异常. 我们称这种现象为余域缠绕并认定为跨域正常-异常引导GAD的关键瓶颈(见图一)。

blocks.en: Figure 1 : t-SNE visualization of residual features before and after DART. Colors denote defect types, while marker shapes denote source domains. (a) In the SotA baseline, residuals are fragmented and strongly influenced by domain identity: samples with the same defect type appear in multiple separated regions, while different defect types often overlap. blocks.en: This issue relates GAD to domain adaptation [ 13 , 14 ] , where domain-specific representations are known to generalize poorly under distribution shift. However, GAD requires more than feature alignment: normal-abnormal residuals must be disentangled, since anomaly cues and domain-specific factors are mixed within the same representation.
blocks.zh: 这一问题涉及GAD与域名的适应[13,14],据了解,域名的具体表述一般在分配上变化不佳。 然而,GAD要求的不仅仅是特征相接:正常-异常的残基必须被分解出来,因为异常提示和特定领域因素在同一代表范围内混合.

blocks.en: We view this objective through an information-theoretic lens: the anomaly component 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} should retain information about the anomaly label Y Y , while minimizing information about the domain D D , with reconstruction preserving the original residual. This motivates DART (Domain-Agnostic Residual Transfer) , a plug-in framework for normal-abnormal GAD. DART combines two components. First, a Residual Disentanglement Module (RDM) splits a residual into an anomaly-relevant component 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} and a domain-specific component 𝐫 d \mathbf{r}_{d} using sufficiency, adversarial invariance, and reconstruction losses. Second, Cross-Domain Meta-Training (CDMT) forms episodes with references and queries from different source domains to make this separation learnable. RDM provides the mechanism for suppressing domain information, while CDMT provides the cross-domain signal needed to learn it.
blocks.zh: 我们通过一个信息-理论镜头来看待这一目标:异常组件 r a\ mathbf{r}_{a} 应该保留关于异常标签 Y Y 的信息,同时尽量减少关于域 D D 的信息, 重建则保留原有的剩余. 这激发了DART(域-不可知残余转移),这是正常-异常GAD的插件框架. DART结合了两个组件. 首先,一个残留分解模块(RDM)利用充足性、对抗性变化和重建损失,将一个残留分解成一个与异常相关的组件r a mathb{r}_{a}和一个域特定组件r d\mathb{r}_{d}。 其次,跨域Meta-Training(CDMT)会用来自不同源域的参考和查询来形成集,使这种分离变得可以学习. RDM提供了压制域信息的机制,而CDMT则提供了学习域信息所需的跨域信号.

blocks.en: RDM operates between residual computation and the downstream detection head, making DART independent of a specific architecture. We apply it to NAGL [ 12 ] , the current normal-abnormal guided GAD baseline, and to adapted versions of InCTRL [ 10 ] and ResAD [ 11 ] .
blocks.zh: RDM在剩余计算和下游检测头之间运行,使DART独立于特定架构. 我们把它应用于NAGL [12],即目前正常-异常引导的GAD基线,并应用于InCTRL [10]和ResAD [11] 的改编版本.

blocks.en: Our contributions are threefold: (i) we identify residual domain entanglement as a bottleneck in normal-abnormal guided GAD; (ii) we propose DART, combining RDM and CDMT to learn anomaly-relevant, domain-agnostic residuals; and (iii) we evaluate it on MVTec AD, VisA, and BraTS across NAGL and two adapted residual-based GAD baselines, showing consistent image-level gains and competitive localization performance under cross-domain transfer.
blocks.zh: 我们的贡献有三个方面:(一) 我们确定剩余域缠绕是正常-异常引导的GAD中的一个瓶颈;(二) 我们提出DART,结合RDM和CDMT学习异常相关,域-不可知的后遗症;(三) 我们在MVTec AD, VisA和BRATS上对它进行评价,跨越NAGL和两个经过调整的基于后遗症的GAD基线,在跨域转移下显示一致的图像水平收益和竞争性本地化性能.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Generalist Anomaly Detection. Visual anomaly detection is mostly single-domain, using memory banks [ 5 , 15 ] , reconstruction [ 16 ] , knowledge distillation [ 8 , 17 ] , normalizing flows [ 7 , 6 ] , or meta-learning [ 18 ] . Few- and zero-shot methods [ 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 ] and generative augmentation [ 24 ] reduce supervision, but often rely on category-specific adaptation or normal-only references. Generalist Anomaly Detection (GAD) instead trains one model on source domains and transfers it to unseen targets without fine-tuning. InCTRL [ 10 ] learns in-context residuals from few-shot normal prompts, while ResAD [ 11 ] models residual feature distributions to reduce class-specific variation. Both rely on normal references, and recent work mines additional normality from the query itself [ 25 ] . NAGL [ 12 ] introduced normal-abnormal guided GAD, exploiting abnormal references via residual mining and anomaly feature learning. We build on this setting but address a different limitation: normal-abnormal residuals can remain entangled with domain-specific information, limiting cross-domain transfer.
blocks.zh: 通论异常检测. 视觉异常探测多为单域,使用记忆库[5,15],重建[16],知识分馏[8,17],使流量正常化[7,6],或元-学习[18]. 少有和零射出的方法[19,20,21,22,23]和基因增生[24]会减少监督,但往往依赖于特定类别的调整或仅能正常引用. 一般反常检测(GAD)则在源域上训练出一款模型,并在不作微调的情况下将其转移到隐形目标. InCTRL [10] 从几发平平平的提示中学习到内文本残存,而ResAD [11] 模式后剩余特征分布以减少类特异性. 两者都依赖正常的参考,最近的工作地雷也从查询本身中增加了正常程度[25]。 NAGL [12]引入了正常-异常引导的GAD,通过剩余采矿和异常特征学习利用了异常引用. 我们基于这一设定,但解决了不同的限制:正常-异常的剩余物仍可被特定域的信息所缠绕,限制了跨域转移.

blocks.en: Domain-Invariant Representation Learning. Domain adaptation theory links target error to source error and cross-domain divergence [ 13 ] , motivating domain-adversarial training with gradient reversal [ 14 ] and domain generalization methods [ 26 , 27 ] . Disentanglement approaches separate invariant and domain-specific factors using adversarial [ 28 , 29 ] or variational [ 30 ] objectives, while meta-learning studies cross-domain episodes for few-shot generalization [ 31 , 32 , 33 , 34 ] . Unlike these works, DART neither disentangles raw features nor assumes target-domain access during training. It disentangles normal-abnormal residuals, separating anomaly-relevant changes from domain-specific factors for unseen-domain GAD.

blocks.en: Our key observation is that residuals are not purely anomaly-specific: they also encode domain-dependent factors such as texture, geometry, and illumination. We call this residual domain entanglement . Under domain shift, these nuisance components can transfer poorly, causing spurious activations or missed detections in unseen target domains.
blocks.zh: 我们的关键观察是,残留物并非纯粹的异常特异性:它们还编码了由域所依赖的因素,如纹理,几何和发光等. 我们称之为余域缠绕 在域位转移下,这些扰动元件可能转移不良,导致在看不见的目标域中出现虚假活化或被错失检测.

blocks.en: RDM alone does not guarantee that 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} becomes domain-invariant. If training episodes are formed within a single domain, domain-specific cues in the residual remain predictive, and the model can achieve low training error without removing them. In the limiting case, the anomaly branch can simply preserve the full residual, i.e., 𝐫 a ≈ 𝐫 \mathbf{r}_{a}\approx\mathbf{r} , while still achieving strong in-domain performance.

blocks.en: CDMT addresses this issue by constructing cross-domain episodes with probability p cross p_{\mathrm{cross}} : the reference set 𝒮 \mathcal{S} is sampled from domain D i D_{i} , while the query 𝐱 q \mathbf{x}_{q} is sampled from a different domain D j D_{j} , with i ≠ j i\neq j . Under this regime, domain-specific cues in the residual become unreliable for prediction, and the model is forced to rely on the transferable component of 𝐫 \mathbf{r} instead. Combined with the adversarial invariance loss, CDMT provides the supervision needed to make the intended decomposition learnable in practice. In this way, RDM defines how residual information is separated, while CDMT provides the cross-domain signal that makes this separation meaningful.

blocks.en: CDMT protocol & reference selection. In CDMT, a domain is an object category, not a dataset: 𝒟 S \mathcal{D}_{S} holds 15 categories when MVTec AD is the source and 12 when VisA is, and the target dataset is held out entirely (App. A.2 ). Each episode draws references from a source category D i D_{i} and the query from a category D j D_{j} (Table 1 ); episodes are same-domain ( D j = D i D_{j}{=}D_{i} ) during a T w = 5 T_{w}{=}5 -epoch warmup, after which the cross-domain probability ramps linearly to p max = 0.3 p_{\max}{=}0.3 (Sec. 3.3). blocks.en:
Host methods & baselines. We integrate DART into NAGL [ 12 ] , the current normal-abnormal guided GAD baseline, and into adapted versions of two residual-based GAD methods: InCTRL [ 10 ] and ResAD [ 11 ] . This allows us to evaluate whether residual disentanglement improves both an existing normal-abnormal method and normal-only GAD pipelines extended with abnormal references.
We compare against two groups of methods. The first comprises established few-shot AD approaches that use normal references only : SPADE [ 37 ] , WinCLIP [ 20 ] , and PromptAD [ 21 ] , along with the vanilla (unmodified) versions of our three host methods InCTRL, ResAD, and NAGL. The second group evaluates the effect of introducing abnormal references: for each host method we report +Inv , which naively incorporates the abnormal reference without disentanglement, and +DART , which applies the full RDM pipeline. Comparing vanilla → \to +Inv isolates the value of abnormal access alone, while comparing +Inv → \to +DART isolates the contribution of residual disentanglement.
blocks.zh:
主机方法与基线. 我们把DART整合到目前正常-异常的GAD基准NAGL [12] 中,并整合到两种基于剩余GAD方法的可修改版本:InCTRL [10]和ResAD [11]. 这使得我们可以评估残余分解是否既改进了现有的常态-异常方法,又改进了仅以异常参考方式延伸的GAD管道。
我们比较了两组方法。 第一类包括既定的几发自动取款方式,仅使用正常的参考文献:SPADE [37],WinCLIP [20],以及ExponalAD [21],以及我们三种主机方法InCTRL、ResAD和NAGL的香草(未修改)版本。 第二组评价引入异常引用的效果:对于我们报告的每个主机方法+Inv,它天真地包含了异常引用而不被分解,以及+DART,它应用了完整的RDM管道. 比较香草 →\ to + Inv 单独隔离异常访问的值,而比较 +Inv →\ to +DART 则隔离剩余分解的贡献.

blocks.en: DART configuration. DART operates on the raw residual produced by each host method and leaves the downstream detection head unchanged. RDM contains an anomaly encoder E a E_{a} , a domain encoder E d E_{d} , a reconstruction decoder G G , and a domain classifier C d C_{d} trained through gradient reversal. The objective combines anomaly sufficiency, adversarial domain invariance, and residual reconstruction. Training follows CDMT, with cross-domain episodes sampled from source domains only; target domains are never used for training, validation, or checkpoint selection. Host-method parameters remain frozen, and at inference only E a E_{a} and the host detection head are retained. Implementation details and hyperparameters are provided in the supplementary material.

blocks.en: 5 Results
blocks.zh: 5 结果

blocks.en: Table 2 compares DART against existing methods on the MVTec AD and VisA benchmarks. NAGL+DART achieves the highest image-level AUROC across all shot settings on both datasets. On MVTec AD, NAGL+DART reaches 95.93%, 96.62%, and 97.34% at N 1 N^{1} , N 2 N^{2} , and N 4 N^{4} respectively, consistently outperforming all baselines including PromptAD (94.6%, 95.7%, 96.6%) and vanilla NAGL. On VisA, where the domain gap from the MVTec-trained source is largest, the improvements are more pronounced: NAGL+DART achieves 89.72% at N 2 + A 1 N^{2}{+}A^{1} , a +1.82% gain over vanilla NAGL (87.90%), and 91.29% at N 4 + A 1 N^{4}{+}A^{1} (+0.99% over NAGL). This pattern, larger gains under larger domain shift, is consistent with our hypothesis that residual domain entanglement is the primary bottleneck, and that its impact scales with the dissimilarity between source and target distributions. Gains are also most pronounced at low-shot settings ( N 1 N^{1} , N 2 N^{2} ) where fewer target-domain references make cross-domain transfer most critical, and gradually narrow as additional references partially compensate for entanglement.
blocks.zh: 表2比较了DART与MVTec AD和VisA基准上的现有方法. NAGL+DART在两个数据集的所有镜头设置中实现最高的图像级别AUROC. 在MVTec AD上,NAGL+DART分别达到95.93%,96.62%和97.34%在N1 N^{1},N2 N^{2}和N4 N^{4}持续地超过所有基准,包括SournalAD(94.6%,95.7%,96.6%)和香草 NAGL. 在VisA上,MVTec训练出源的域间隙最大,改进更显著: NAGL+DART在N 2 + A 1 N^{2}{+}A^{1} → 得到89.72%,比香草 NAGL(87.90%)获得+1.82%的增益;在N 4 + A 1 N^{4}{+}A^{1}(比 NAGL多0.99%)获得91.29%的增益. 这种模式,在更大的域位转移下更大的收益,符合我们的假设,即剩余域缠绕是主要的瓶颈,其影响尺度与源与目标分布的相去不远. 增益在低镜头设置(N 1 N^{1},N 2 N^{2})中也最为明显,其中较少的目标域引用使得跨域传输最为关键,并逐渐缩小,因为额外的引用部分地补偿了缠绕.

blocks.en: At the pixel level, NAGL+DART matches or improves upon vanilla NAGL on PRO and P-AUROC across most settings, while simultaneously achieving the best image-level metrics. This indicates that disentanglement does not sacrifice localization quality for classification gains, a common failure mode when modifying residual representations. The pixel-level F1-max shows occasional small drops ( e.g. , − - 1.16 at N 1 N^{1} on VisA), which we attribute to F1’s threshold sensitivity rather than to a systematic degradation, as both P-AUROC and PRO remain competitive.
blocks.zh: 在像素层面,NAGL+DART在PRO和P-AUROC上与香草NAGL相匹配或改进,同时实现最佳的图像级度量. 这表明分解不会牺牲分类收益的本地化质量,这是修改剩余表述时常见的失败模式. 像素级的F1-max显示偶尔会有小的下降(例如:-- 1.16 在VisA上的N 1 N^{1}),我们将此归因于F1的阈值灵敏度而不是系统性的降解,因为P-AUROC和PRO都保持竞争力.

blocks.en: Disentanglement vs. naive abnormal access. The +Inv rows in Table 2 separate access to abnormal references from disentangling them. Naive integration is unreliable and often harmful: ResAD+Inv loses − - 3.0 I-AUROC on MVTec AD and − - 6.5 on VisA at N 1 N^{1} (PRO up to − - 6.0), and InCTRL+Inv swings from +0.42 at N 1 N^{1} to − - 1.22 at N 4 N^{4} without ever producing spatially coherent pixel-level maps. DART recovers and exceeds vanilla performance in the same settings, and the +Inv → \to +DART gap widens with domain shift: +6.19 I-AUROC on VisA at N 1 N^{1} (79.87% vs. 86.06%), growing to +9.85 at N 4 N^{4} (80.29% vs. 90.14%). Residual disentanglement, not mere abnormal access, drives the improvement; the full per-category breakdown is in App. A.8 .

DART在同一环境下恢复并超过香草性能,并随着域位转移,+Inv →\to +DART差距会扩大:+6.19 I-AUROC on VisA at 1 N^{1}(79.87%对86.06%),在N 4. N^{4}(80.29%对90.14%)增长到+9.85. 残余的分解,而不仅仅是非正常的取用,推动了改进;每个类别的全部分解情况载于App.A.8.。

blocks.en: DART as a general plug-in. RDM operates on the residual 𝐫 \mathbf{r} as a method-agnostic interface, requiring no modification to detection heads or method-specific hyperparameter tuning beyond λ adv \lambda_{\mathrm{adv}} and λ recon \lambda_{\mathrm{recon}} . This design choice is validated by the breadth of host methods: NAGL mines attention-based residuals over ViT patch tokens, InCTRL computes multi-layer in-context residuals from CLIP features, and ResAD learns distributional deviations via normalizing flows on WideResNet features, three substantially different architectures, all of which improve under DART without any method-specific adaptation. A notable emergent capability is pixel-level localization in InCTRL, which originally reported no segmentation metrics: disentangling the residual produces spatially meaningful anomaly maps as a byproduct, achieving P-AUROC of 94.52–95.71% on MVTec AD across shot settings.
blocks.zh: DART作为通用插座. RDM在所剩的 r\ mathbf{r} 上作为方法不可知的界面运行, 不需要修改检测头或方法特有的超参数调用, 超越了 \\ adv\ lambda\ mathrm{ adv} 和 &\ recon\ 。 这种设计选择通过主机方法的宽度得到验证: NAGL 矿井以注意力为主的残基在ViT补丁符号之上,InCTRL从CLIP特性中计算出多层内文本残基,ResAD通过将流量在WideResNet特性上正常化来学习分布偏差,三种结构大相径庭,在DART下都得到了改进而没有任何方法特定的改造. 一种显著的出现能力是InCTRL中的像素级本地化,它最初报告没有分块度量:将剩余物分解产生具有空间意义的异常地图作为副产品,在MVTec AD上实现94.52-95.71%的P-AUROC跨镜头设置.

blocks.en: Efficiency. DART’s overhead is modest and front-loaded: training adds 3.1–20.1M parameters and ≈ {\approx} 1 GPU-hour per setting on a single RTX4090, incurred once on source domains with the host frozen. At inference only E a E_{a} is retained (+0.82M for InCTRL, +0.89M for NAGL, +9.06M for ResAD) and operates on low-dimensional residuals, so runtime overhead is negligible (Table 5 ).

blocks.en: 5.1 Industrial-to-Medical Transfer
blocks.zh: 5.1 工业对医疗转移

blocks.en: Table 3 evaluates DART on the most challenging setting, MVTec AD → \to BraTS (industrial defects → \to brain-tumor MRI). DART improves all three host methods on this extreme domain shift in nearly every setting, with gains substantially larger than those on industrial benchmarks. InCTRL+DART achieves the most striking improvement: +13.28% image-level AUROC at N 1 N^{1} (65.20% → \to 78.48%) and +7.61% at N 4 N^{4} (69.89% → \to 77.50%), while ResAD+DART improves by +5.20% at N 2 N^{2} and NAGL+DART improves at both N 2 N^{2} (+0.25%) and N 4 N^{4} (+0.99%). The gains extend to localization: InCTRL+DART raises pixel-level AUROC from 83.65% to 87.67% at N 1 N^{1} and from 90.06% to 93.85% at N 4 N^{4} . The single exception is NAGL+DART at N 1 N^{1} , where a pixel-level drop (93.00% → \to 90.33%) lowers the mean despite a slightly higher image-level AUROC; with two or more normal references it improves both. The magnified gains on BraTS support our core claim that the impact of residual domain entanglement scales with the severity of the domain shift.

blocks.en: Architecture (Table 3 b). Replacing the MLP encoder with a linear projection causes a sharp drop on VisA ( − - 7.35 I-AUROC) while leaving MVTec-AD nearly unchanged, demonstrating that non-linear capacity is essential specifically for cross-domain disentanglement where the domain gap is larger. blocks.en: Disentanglement strategy (Table 3 c). Both adversarial-only and orthogonality-only baselines degrade below vanilla on both datasets (up to − - 1.74 MVTec-AD, − - 2.02 VisA). Adversarial-only training suppresses domain information but lacks a constraint to preserve anomaly signal, allowing E a E_{a} to collapse. Orthogonality-only training enforces geometric independence but permits anomaly-relevant directions to migrate into 𝐫 d \mathbf{r}_{d} . DART’s joint objective resolves both: ℒ suf \mathcal{L}_{\text{suf}} prevents collapse, ℒ recon \mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}} ensures completeness, and ℒ adv \mathcal{L}_{\text{adv}} drives genuine domain suppression under these constraints. The +2.89 gap over the best single-objective baseline confirms that no proper subset achieves the same effect.

blocks.en: Residual vs. feature space (Table 4 f, Fig. 3 ). DART-F, which applies disentanglement in backbone feature space, degrades performance ( − - 0.54 vs. vanilla) while DART improves it (+1.15). Silhouette analysis of the same 640-d residuals (identical normalization, no detector in the loop) reveals why: DART-F amplifies domain separation (0.246 → \to 0.611) because backbone features are domain-discriminative by pretraining design and a lightweight plug-in cannot override this geometry, whereas in residual space domain information is only incidental and DART suppresses it (0.246 → \to 0.192). Relabeling the same residuals by defect type (computed within each category and averaged, as MVTec AD defect types are category-specific), the silhouette rises from 0.08 to 0.25 under DART while DART-F stalls at 0.10: domain identity becomes a weaker axis of variation in 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} and defect identity a stronger one, demotion rather than deletion of domain information, and we do not claim perfect invariance. Anomaly preservation is enforced structurally: the frozen host head reads only 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} , so any direction it uses cannot be discarded without paying ℒ suf \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{suf}} ; removing ℒ suf \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{suf}} indeed yields this degenerate solution, invariance by discarding, falling below the unmodified host (Table 4 e).

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we identified residual domain entanglement as a fundamental bottleneck limiting cross-domain transfer in normal-abnormal guided Generalist Anomaly Detection. To address this, we proposed DART, a plug-in framework comprising a Residual Disentanglement Module (RDM) and Cross-Domain Meta-Training (CDMT) that decomposes residuals into domain-agnostic anomaly components and domain-specific components. Extensive experiments across three host methods, three benchmarks, and three few-shot settings demonstrated that DART consistently improves cross-domain detection performance, with gains scaling with the severity of the domain shift (industrial-to-medical transfer). While adding 3–20M training-time parameters (0.8–9.1M at inference), DART delivers gains over vanilla (up to +1.82% I-AUROC on industrial benchmarks and +13.28% on medical transfer), whereas naive abnormal integration (+Inv) often degrades performance (e.g., − - 6.5% I-AUROC for ResAD on VisA), making DART’s net gain over +Inv as high as +9.85%. Ablation studies confirmed that all components are jointly necessary and that disentanglement must operate in residual space. DART assumes at least one abnormal reference at test time, which zero-shot deployments may lack, and our evaluation is restricted to images; extending residual disentanglement to video and time-series anomalies is left to future work.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们确定,剩余域缠绕是限制在正常-异常通用探测中跨域转移的根本瓶颈。 为了解决这个问题,我们提议了DART这一插件框架,其中包括一个残余分解模块(RDM)和跨域Meta-Training(CDMT),将残余分解成域-不可知异常组件和域特有组件. 跨越三种主机方法、三种基准和三种几发设置的广泛实验表明,DART不断提高跨域检测性能,其收益随域转移(从工业到医疗转移)的严重程度而扩大。 虽然增加了3–20M培训时间参数(推断为0.8–9.1M),但DART比香草(在工业基准上达到+1.82%的I-AUROC,在医疗转移上达到+13.28%)带来收益,而天真异常融合(+Inv)往往会降低性能(例如----6.5%的I-AUROC在VisA上的ResAD),使得DART的净收益高于+Inv,高达+9.85%. 校正研究证实,所有部件都是共同必需的,分解必须在剩余空间进行。 DART假设在测试时至少有一个非正常的参考,而零发部署可能缺乏这种参考,我们的评价仅限于图像;将剩余分解扩展到视频和时间序列异常留待未来工作.

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The claims in the Abstract and Section 1 are supported by the results in Table 2 , Table 3 and the ablations in Section 5.2 ; the limitations are stated in the Conclusion. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Limitations are stated at the end of the Conclusion (requirement of at least one abnormal reference at test time; image-only evaluation) and discussed further in Appendix A.6 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [N/A] Justification: This paper does not include theoretical results. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Protocol, host methods, and the DART configuration are described in Section 4 ; architectures, hyperparameters, the CDMT curriculum, reference-selection and leakage controls are given in Appendices A.1 – A.2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Code is made available at https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART (linked in the Abstract), with instructions to reproduce the main results. MVTec AD, VisA, and BraTS are public benchmarks, cited in Section 4 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Please see Section 4 and Appendix A.1 (optimizer, schedule, loss weights, curriculum, validation and checkpoint selection on source domains only). Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: NAGL and NAGL+DART results are averaged over three independent seeds controlling the few-shot reference sampling, with 1-sigma standard deviations below 0.8 I-AUROC and 0.5 P-AUROC in all settings; the reported gains exceed these margins. InCTRL and ResAD follow the single-run protocol of their original papers. See Appendix A.3 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Compute is reported in the Efficiency paragraph of the main text and in the Efficiency Analysis paragraph and Table 5 of Appendix A.1 : a single NVIDIA RTX4090 (24 GB), ≈ {\approx} 1 GPU-hour per setting, and 100–150 GPU-hours in total. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We have read the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and confirm that our research complies with these ethical standards. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Please see the Social Impacts paragraph in Appendix A.6 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The released models are anomaly detectors for industrial and medical benchmark images and pose no such risks. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: All datasets (MVTec AD, VisA, BraTS) and host methods (InCTRL, ResAD, NAGL) are publicly released by their authors under their respective licenses and are cited in the paper; we use them unmodified for research purposes. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The released code is documented in the repository ( https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART ): training and evaluation instructions, the evaluation protocol, and an MIT license. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: Our paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: Our paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. blocks.zh: 1. 联合国 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是] 说明: 《摘要》和第1节中的索赔得到表2、表3和第5.2节中的结果的支持;这些限制在结论中作了说明。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指抽象和导言不包括文件中提出的要求。 抽象和/或导言应明确说明所提出的主张,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 [否]或[否/A]对这个问题的答复不会为审议者所看好。 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相匹配,并反映在多大程度上可以期望将结果归纳到其他环境中。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 说明:在结论末尾说明限制(试验时至少需要一次异常的参考;只进行图像评价),并在附录A.6中进一步讨论。 • 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另设"限制"一栏. 文件应该指出任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设被违反的结果如何有力(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何被违反以及会产生什么影响。 作者应反思所提出主张的范围,例如,如果只在几个数据集上或用几个运行来测试这种做法。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,应当加以阐述。 作者应思考影响该方法执行的因素。 例如,一面相识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像取自于低照明时可能表现不佳. 或语音到文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论拟议算法的计算效率,以及它们如何用数据集大小进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的方法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会把完全诚实的局限性作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中没有承认的局限性。 作者应运用最佳判断,并承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社区完整性的准则方面起重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚有关限制的诚实行为。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[不详]理由: 本文不包括理论成果. 指导方针: 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括理论结果. 二. 支助 纸上所有定理,公式和证明,都应该编号并相互参照. 二. 支助 • 所有假设均应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在正文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证明草图来提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是]说明理由:第4节介绍了协议、东道方方法和DART配置;附录A.1-A.2介绍了架构、超参数、CDMT课程、参考选择和渗漏控制。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是新模型(如:大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(如:有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示等). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 如补充材料所描述的那样,该文件是否提供了公开查阅数据和代码的机会,并提供了忠实复制主要实验结果的充分指示? 答复: [是] 理由: 代码见https://github.com/aqeeelmirza/DART。 (在"文摘"中链接),并指示复制主要结果. MVTec AD、VisA和BratS是公共基准,引自第4节。 · 答案[N/A]是指纸张不包括需要密码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 文件不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而被拒绝,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). 二. 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何取用原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本来复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验可以复制,它们应该说明哪些实验从剧本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为了保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的资料(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(例如数据分解、超参数、如何选择、优化者类型等)? 答复:[是] 说明: 请参看第4节和附录A.1(优化、时间表、减重、课程、验证和仅在源域选择检查站)。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 试验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便评估结果,使之有意义。 详细情况可通过守则、附录或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告的错误是否包含适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验的统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 说明:NAGL和NAGL+DART的结果平均在三个独立种子上进行,控制了几发参考取样,所有情况下的1-西格玛标准差低于0.8 I-AUROC和0.5 P-AUROC;报告的增益超过了这些幅度。 InCTRL和ResAD遵循其原始论文的单跑协议. 见附录A.3。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果结果附有出错栏、置信间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕获的可变因素(例如,列车/测试分拆、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算出错栏的方法应加以解释(封闭表单公式、调用库函数、靴子等) • 应给出假设(例如,通常分布式错误)。 应明确出错栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准出错. ^ 报告1-西格玛出错栏是好的,但应该说明这一点。 撰文者最好报告2-相格马出错栏,而不是说如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,他们有96%的CI。 二. 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称错误栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负出错率). 二. 支助 如果在表格或图中报告出错栏,作者应在正文中解释其计算方式并参考正文中的相应数字或表格. 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 说明:计算在正文中的效率段落和附录A.1中的效率分析段落和表5中报告:单NVIDIA RTX4090(24GB),\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\\每设定1GPU小时,以及总共100~150GPU小时。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额并估计总计算数。 本文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文所报道的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写入论文). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复: [是] 理由: 我们阅读了《新IPS道德守则》,确认我们的研究符合这些道德标准。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应当解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例而得到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和负面社会影响? 答复:[是] 说明: 请见附录A.6的社会影响段落。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件不讨论社会影响。 二. 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(如:造谣、制造假相、监视)、公平考虑(如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以使人们能训练出能更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ 作者应考虑在技术被作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术被作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及因(有意或无意)滥用技术而可能造成的损害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行严密释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测滥用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中吸取教训的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布滥用风险高的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或被刮去的数据集)而采取的保障措施? blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.

The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. blocks.zh: 说明:第4节介绍了协议、主机方法和DART配置;附录A.1 – A.2介绍了架构、超参数、CDMT课程、参考选择和渗漏控制。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括实验。 如果论文包括了实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使该文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或核实而采取的步骤。 • 视贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一种具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人有可能用同样的数据集复制该模型,或者提供对模型的取用. 总论. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一目的的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. 二. 支助 虽然NeurIPS并不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交文件提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范架构,文件应清楚而全面地描述该架构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大型语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者说明它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 就闭源模型而言,可能以某种方式(例如,对已注册的用户)限制对模型的访问,但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. blocks.en: We reproduce each host method following its original protocol to ensure that observed gains are attributable to DART rather than implementation differences. InCTRL [ 10 ] uses a frozen OpenCLIP ViT-B/16-plus-240 backbone at 240 × 240 240{\times}240 resolution, computing multi-layer patch-level cosine distance maps and image-level residual vectors between query and normal prompts. The learnable adapter ψ \psi and classifier η \eta are trained with binary focal loss while the CLIP backbone remains frozen. Full architectural details are provided in § A.4.1 . ResAD [ 11 ] employs a frozen WideResNet-50 with multi-layer feature aggregation. blocks.en: InCTRL and ResAD are originally designed for normal-only references. We adapt them for the N k + A 1 N^{k}{+}A^{1} setting as follows: • InCTRL+DART: The abnormal reference is passed through the frozen CLIP visual encoder alongside normal prompts. The residual between abnormal and normal token embeddings at each layer is computed analogously to the query-normal residual (Eq. 10 ), producing an abnormal-normal residual tensor. This tensor is fed into RDM, which outputs 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} . The disentangled residual is then fused with the existing query-normal residual via concatenation before the scoring head. • ResAD+DART: The abnormal reference features are extracted from the frozen WideResNet backbone. Per-patch residuals between abnormal and normal features are computed via nearest-neighbor subtraction (Eq. 12 ). These residuals are fed into RDM to produce 𝐫 a \mathbf{r}_{a} , which is concatenated with the original query-normal residual features before the Feature Constraintor and normalizing flow. • +Inv baseline: The same abnormal reference integration is performed, but without RDM, the raw abnormal-normal residual is concatenated directly. This isolates the contribution of disentanglement from the benefit of abnormal access.

blocks.en: Tab. 5 summarizes the efficiency of each host method and the overhead introduced by DART, distinguishing training-time from inference-time cost. The full RDM adds 3.1M, 4.2M, and 20.1M parameters for InCTRL, NAGL, and ResAD respectively during training; at inference, only the anomaly encoder E a E_{a} is retained (0.82M, 0.89M, and 9.06M), while the domain encoder, reconstruction decoder, and domain classifier are training-only components discarded after learning the residual decomposition. Training requires approximately 1 GPU-hour per setting (30 epochs on a single NVIDIA RTX4090 GPU) since the host backbone is fully frozen, and this cost is incurred only once: the learned module transfers to unseen target domains without any further optimization. Inference overhead is negligible as the RDM operates only on low-dimensional residual features. All results are reported for 1, 2 and 4 shot settings; total compute for all experiments (3 host methods × \times 3 datasets × \times 3 shot settings, with 3 seeds for NAGL) is approximately 100-150 GPU-hours on NVIDIA RTX4090 GPUs (24 GB VRAM).

blocks.en: A.2 Leakage Controls
blocks.zh: A.2 泄漏控制

blocks.en: A central concern in cross-domain anomaly detection is information leakage between training and evaluation. We enforce three levels of isolation, all derived from the leave-one-dataset-out design.
blocks.zh: 跨领域异常发现中的一个中心问题是培训与评价之间的信息泄露。 我们实施三级隔离 都来自一个数据组的设计

blocks.en: Category-level isolation. The evaluation category never appears as a source domain during training, since the entire dataset it belongs to is excluded from 𝒟 S \mathcal{D}_{S} .
blocks.zh: 类别级隔离. 在培训期间评价类别从未作为源域出现,因为它所属的整个数据集被排除在DS\mathcal{D}_{S}之外.

blocks.en: Dataset-level isolation. Categories within the same dataset share acquisition pipeline, lighting, sensor resolution, and annotation conventions. Excluding individual test categories while retaining other categories from the same dataset would leak domain-specific appearance statistics into training. Our leave-one-dataset-out construction eliminates this.
blocks.zh: 数据集级隔离. 在同一数据集内的类别:共享获取管道、照明、传感器分辨率和注释常规。 将单个测试类别排除在外,同时保留同一数据集中的其他类别,将使特定领域外观统计数据泄露到培训中。 我们的一一数据组的建造 消除了这一点。

blocks.en: Support-set isolation. The few-shot reference images used at test time are drawn from the standard evaluation split of D k D_{k} and are not observed during training under any sampling scheme.
blocks.zh: 支持设置隔离. 试验时使用的几发参考图像取自Dk D_{k}的标准评价分数,在任何取样计划下在训练中都没有观察到.

blocks.en: Together, these conditions guarantee that performance on 𝒟 T \mathcal{D}_{T} reflects genuine generalization from 𝒟 S \mathcal{D}_{S} .
blocks.zh: 这些条件共同保证了在 D T\ mathcal{ D}_{T} 上的性能能够反映从 D S\ mathcal{ D}_{S} 中真正的概括.

blocks.en: A.3 Statistical Significance
blocks.zh: A.3 统计意义

blocks.en: NAGL and NAGL+DART results are averaged over three independent seeds controlling the few-shot reference sampling, with standard deviations consistently below 0.8% for I-AUROC and 0.5% for P-AUROC across all datasets and shot settings; the observed DART improvements (e.g., +0.39% I-AUROC on MVTec at N 1 N^{1} , +1.82% on VisA at N 2 N^{2} ) exceed these margins by a substantial factor. InCTRL and ResAD follow the single-run evaluation protocol of their original papers [ 10 , 11 ] ; for these backbones, robustness of DART gains is evidenced by their consistency across all shot settings and the majority of per-category results (Tables 8 – 25 ).
blocks.zh: NAGL和NAGL+DART结果平均在3个独立种子上控制了几发参考采样,I-AUROC的标准偏差一直低于0.8%,P-AUROC在所有数据集和镜头设置中均低于0.5%;观察到的DART改进(例如N 1 N^{1}的MVTec上的+0.39% I-AUROC,N 2 N^{2}的VisA上的+1.82%)超过了这些边际。 InCTRL和ResAD遵循其原始论文的单跑评价协议[10,11];对这些骨干而言,DART收益的稳健性体现在所有镜头设置和大多数每类结果的一致性上(表8-25)。

blocks.en: A potential source of confusion arises from the role of the abnormal reference ℱ a \mathcal{F}_{a} in residual computation. We clarify this here.

blocks.en: As shown in Fig. 2 , the host residual operator computes 𝐫 = ℛ ⁡ ( 𝐟 q , ℱ n , ℱ a ) , \mathbf{r}=\mathcal{R}(\mathbf{f}_{q};\,\mathcal{F}_{n},\,\mathcal{F}_{a}), (15) where 𝐟 q \mathbf{f}_{q} is the query feature and { ℱ n , ℱ a } \{\mathcal{F}_{n},\mathcal{F}_{a}\} are the normal and abnormal reference features. This single residual 𝐫 \mathbf{r} is the input to RDM. The exact form of ℛ \mathcal{R} is method-specific: NAGL and ResAD compute the abnormal-normal residual via patch-level nearest-neighbour subtraction of ℱ a \mathcal{F}_{a} against ℱ n \mathcal{F}_{n} , while InCTRL computes it as a patch-level cosine distance map and an image-level residual vector across transformer layers. In all cases, 𝐫 \mathbf{r} encodes the deviation of the abnormal reference from the normal reference, and RDM receives this as input regardless of how the host method produces it, making DART a true plug-in framework.

blocks.en: Within ℛ \mathcal{R} , ℱ n \mathcal{F}_{n} provides the normal baseline and ℱ a \mathcal{F}_{a} acts as a directional anchor, it encodes what anomaly looks like in the reference domain. Together, they orient 𝐫 \mathbf{r} so that its magnitude and direction reflect how the query deviates from normal in the direction of the reference anomaly . This is precisely why 𝐫 \mathbf{r} carries domain entanglement: both the transferable anomaly pattern and the domain-specific texture of ℱ a \mathcal{F}_{a} are embedded in 𝐫 \mathbf{r} .

blocks.en: A.6 Discussion
blocks.zh: A.6 讨论情况

blocks.en: DART requires at least one abnormal reference sample at test time, which may not always be available in zero-shot scenarios; our experiments also focus solely on image data, and extension to video or time-series modalities remains future work.
blocks.zh: DART在测试时需要至少一个异常的参考样本,这在零镜头情景中可能并不总是可以获得;我们的实验还只注重图像数据,扩展到视频或时间序列模式仍然是今后的工作.

blocks.en: As a plug-in framework for generalist anomaly detection, DART does not raise specific ethical issues or adverse societal effects. All datasets used are publicly available. Qualitative illustrations are derived from industrial product imagery and medical imaging benchmarks, ensuring no violation of personal privacy.
blocks.zh: 作为泛论异常检测的插入框架,DART没有提出具体的伦理问题或不利的社会影响. 所有使用的数据集都公开提供。 定性插图取自工业产品成像和医学成像基准,确保不侵犯个人隐私.

blocks.en: A.7 VisA Domain Entanglement Analysis
blocks.zh: A.7 VisA域包围分析

blocks.en: To empirically validate that residual domain entanglement is the core bottleneck addressed by DART, we visualize the token-level residual space using t-SNE on VisA at k = 2 k{=}2 shots (Figure 4 ). Without DART, residuals form tight clusters organized by domain identity rather than anomaly semantics, confirming that the normal–abnormal difference vector carries substantial domain texture information. With DART, RDM strips the domain-specific component: residuals reorganize into clusters aligned with defect type , grouping semantically similar anomalies across object categories. VisA exhibits particularly strong domain entanglement due to its high intra-class visual variance (structurally complex objects such as PCBs and food items), directly explaining why DART yields larger performance gains on VisA than on MVTec AD.
blocks.zh: 为了在经验上验证残余域缠绕是DART所处理的核心瓶颈,我们用t-SNE在VisA上以k=2 k{=}2 shots(图4)将符号级的残余空间可视化. 没有DART,残基会形成由域名而不是异常语义组织起来的紧凑的集群,确认正常-异常差向量携带了实质性域纹理信息. 通过DART,RDM会将域特有成分剥去:剩余成分重组为与缺陷类型相适应的集群,在对象类别之间组分形成高度相近的异常. VisA因其高级视觉差异(结构复杂物体,如多氯联苯和食品)而表现出特别强的域缠绕,直接解释了为什么DART比MVTec AD产生更大的性能收益。

blocks.en: A.8 Disentanglement Analysis: Vanilla vs. +Inv vs. +DART
blocks.zh: A.8 分离分析:香草对+Inv对+DART

blocks.en: Table 6 provides the full vanilla/+Inv/+DART breakdown for all three host methods on MVTec AD and VisA across all shot settings ( N 1 N^{1} through N 4 N^{4} ), extending the mean-level +Inv comparison now included in Table 2 of the main paper with all twelve metrics and per-metric directional markers.
blocks.zh: 表6列出 MVTec AD和VisA上所有三种主机方法(N 1 N^{1}至N 4 N^{4})的全梵文/+Inv/+DART分解,将平均值+Inv的比较扩展至现在列入主论文表2的所有12个公尺和每分量的方向标记.

blocks.en: Across all three host methods, the +Inv baseline, which incorporates abnormal references without disentanglement, degrades performance relative to vanilla in the majority of settings. The damage is most severe for ResAD, where +Inv drops I-AUROC by − - 3.0% on MVTec AD and − - 6.5% on VisA at N 1 N^{1} , with pixel-level PRO degrading by up to − - 6.0 points. For InCTRL, +Inv is inconsistent: it provides marginal image-level gains at low shots ( N 1 N^{1} : +0.42%, N 2 N^{2} : +0.67%) but degrades at higher shots ( N 4 N^{4} : − - 1.22%). Crucially, +Inv never produces pixel-level metrics for InCTRL, the entangled abnormal residuals generate spatially incoherent activations that prevent meaningful localization. These results confirm our core hypothesis: raw abnormal references carry domain-entangled information that corrupts rather than aids cross-domain detection.
blocks.zh: 在所有三种主机方法中,+Inv基线包含非正常引用而不分解,在大多数设置中相对于香草的性能会降解. 对ResAD来说,破坏最严重,其中+Inv将I-AUROC在MVTec AD上降为--3.0%,在VisA上降为-6.5%在N1NQQ1},像素级的PRO降为--6.0分. 对于InCTRL,+Inv是不一致的:它在低镜头(N 1 N^{1}:+0.42%,N 2 N^{2}:+0.67%)提供边际图像级增益,但在高镜头(N 4 N^{4}:−-1.22%)会降解. 关键是,+Inv从未为InCTRL产生像素级的度量衡,被缠绕的异常残基产生空间不相干活化作用来阻止有意义的本地化. 这些结果证实了我们的核心假设:原始的异常引用携带了域相缠的信息,这些信息腐蚀而不是辅助跨域检测.

blocks.en: In contrast to +Inv, DART improves over vanilla across all three host methods in the large majority of metrics and settings. On InCTRL, DART achieves +0.56% to +1.15% I-AUROC gains on MVTec AD across all shots, while simultaneously enabling pixel-level localization (P-AUROC 94.52–95.71%) that is entirely absent in both vanilla and +Inv. On ResAD, DART recovers the performance destroyed by +Inv and exceeds vanilla (e.g., +0.50% I-AUROC, +1.80% I-AP on VisA at N 2 N^{2} ). On NAGL, which already handles abnormal references natively, DART provides consistent image-level gains on both datasets (up to +1.82% I-AUROC on VisA at N 2 N^{2} ), with pixel-level metrics remaining competitive or improving.
blocks.zh: 与+Inv不同,DART在绝大多数的度量和设置中,在所有三种主机方法中改进了香草. 在 InCTRL上,DART在MVTec AD上实现+0.56%至+1.15%的I-AUROC增益,同时实现像素级本地化(P-AUROC 94.52–95.71%),这在香草和+Inv中都是完全不存在的. 在ResAD上,DART恢复被+Inv所破坏的性能并超越了香草(如:+0.50% I-AUROC,+1.80%的VisA上I-AP在2N^{2}). 在已经从本土处理异常引用的NAGL上,DART在两个数据集上提供一致的图像级增益(最高为+1.82% I-AUROC on VisA at N2 N^{2}),像素级的度量衡仍然具有竞争力或改进.

blocks.en: On MVTec AD (where the VisA-trained model transfers to a moderately different industrial domain), the +Inv → \to +DART gap is moderate. On VisA (where the MVTec-trained model faces a larger domain shift), the gap widens substantially: for example, InCTRL+Inv drops to 79.87% I-AUROC at N 1 N^{1} while InCTRL+DART reaches 86.06%, a gap of +6.19 points. This scaling behavior directly validates that residual disentanglement becomes increasingly critical as the domain gap grows.
blocks.zh: 在MVTec AD(其中由VisA所训练的模型转移到一个中等不同的工业领域)上,+Inv →\ to +DART相差不大. 在VisA上(MVTec所训练的模型面临更大的域位移),差距大幅扩大:例如,InCTRL+Inv在N 1 NQQ1}中下降到79.87% I-AUROC,而InCTRL+DART则达到了86.06%,差距为+6.19分. 这种缩放行为直接验证了剩余分解随着域间隙的增大而变得越来越关键.

blocks.en: A.9 BraTS Disentanglement Analysis
blocks.zh: A.9 BrATS 分离 分析

blocks.en: Table 7(a) provides the full vanilla/+Inv/+DART breakdown on the MVTec AD → \to BraTS transfer, the most extreme domain shift in our evaluation (industrial defects → \to brain tumor MRI).
blocks.zh: 表7(a)提供了MVTec AD →\至BrATS转移(我们评价中最极端的域转移(工业缺陷 →\为脑瘤核磁共振))上的全部香草/+Inv/+DART分解.

blocks.en: On BraTS, the +Inv baseline is again unreliable: InCTRL+Inv provides partial gains at N 1 N^{1} (+3.77% I-AUROC) but degrades sharply at N 4 N^{4} ( − - 3.58%), while ResAD+Inv is consistently neutral or harmful ( − - 2.20% at N 2 N^{2} , − - 1.90% at N 4 N^{4} ). DART, in contrast, produces substantially larger gains than on industrial benchmarks. InCTRL+DART improves by +13.28% I-AUROC at N 1 N^{1} (65.20% → \to 78.48%) and +7.61% at N 4 N^{4} (69.89% → \to 77.50%), representing the largest absolute improvements across all our experiments. ResAD+DART improves by +5.20% at N 2 N^{2} and +3.10% at N 4 N^{4} . NAGL+DART improves consistently at N 2 N^{2} (+0.25%) and N 4 N^{4} (+0.99%).
blocks.zh: 在 BratS 上, + Inv 基线再次不可靠: InCTRL+Inv 提供了 N1 NQQ 1} (+3.77% I-AUROC) 的部分收益,但在 N 4 NQQ 4} (− - 3.58%) 上却急剧降解, 而 ResAD+Inv 则始终是中性或有害的(− 2.20% 在 N 2 NQQQ2},− - 1.90% 在 N 4 NQQ 4} 上). 相比之下,DART的收益远远大于工业基准。 InCTRL+DART改进了+13.28%的I-AUROC在N1 N^{1}(65.20%~\至78.48%)和+7.61%在N4 N^{4}(69.89%~\至77.50%),代表了我们所有实验中最大的绝对改进. ResAD+DART在N2 N^{2}和N4 N^{4}的+3.10%改进了+5.20%. NAGL+DART在N2 N^{2}(+0.25%)和N4 N^{4}(+0.99%)的不断改进.

blocks.en: The industrial-to-medical domain shift is qualitatively different from inter-industrial transfer: the visual appearance, texture statistics, imaging modality, and anomaly semantics all change simultaneously. In this regime, domain-specific information in the residual is not merely unhelpful but actively misleading, industrial texture patterns have no correspondence in MRI data and generate pure noise in the anomaly map. Disentanglement removes this noise entirely, leaving only the domain-agnostic anomaly semantics (structural irregularity, boundary disruption, intensity deviation) that transfer across the modality boundary. The magnitude of improvement directly reflects the magnitude of domain entanglement removed.
blocks.zh: 工业到医疗领域的变化在质量上不同于工业间转移:视觉外观、纹理统计、成像方式和异常语义都同时变化。 在这个制度中,残存物中的特定域信息不仅无济于事,而且具有积极的误导性,工业纹理模式在核磁共振数据中没有对应性,在异常图中产生纯噪音. 分解会完全去除这种噪声,只留下域-不可知异常语义(结构不规则,边界中断,强度偏差),可以跨出模式边界. 改进的程度直接反映了去除域缠绕的程度.

blocks.en: The one setting where DART underperforms on BraTS is NAGL+DART at N 1 N^{1} , where the mean metric drops from 84.66 to 83.35. This is attributable to a pixel-level AUROC drop (93.00 → \to 90.33) while the image-level metric improves slightly (76.32 → \to 76.36). We hypothesize that with only a single normal reference, NAGL’s RM module, which already performs its own residual processing, has insufficient signal for RDM to learn a stable decomposition on this extreme domain shift. At N 2 N^{2} and above, where additional references stabilize the residual computation, DART consistently improves NAGL on BraTS.
blocks.zh: DART在BRATS上表现不佳的设定是N1 NQQ1}的NAGL+DART,其中的平均值从84.66下降到83.35. 这是由于像素级的AUROC下降(93.00~\至90.33),而图像级的度量则略有改善(76.32~\至76.36)。 我们假设,只要一个普通的参考,NAGL的RM模块就已经完成了自身的剩余处理,但是没有足够信号让RDM学会在这个极端域移上稳定分解。 在N 2 N^{2}及以上,在额外参考稳定了剩余计算的情况下,DART在BrATS上不断改进NAGL.
